title: arXiv AI — Tuesday, 3 November 2026: five notable papers
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This inferred ordering uses limited, checkable attention and relevance signals, not a most-read or most-downloaded metric; the papers are very recent and usable citation evidence is limited.

sections.title: Pixel: A Co-Designed Full-Stack Robot System for Learning General-Purpose Mobile Manipulation
sections.abstract: The authors present a co-designed wheeled robot, human/robot demonstration interfaces, whole-body controller, and shared learning pipeline, evaluated on mobile-manipulation behaviors involving dexterity, navigation, and coordination.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper reports an integrated, open-source platform combining robot embodiment, human-aligned demonstrations, shared control, and policy learning; its HTML reports average task progress of 82.0% on three sensorized-human tasks and 78.7% on three robot-teleoperation tasks.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that the wheeled form cannot climb stairs or match a full humanoid’s range and dexterity; the high-level agent is limited to a predefined skill library, and its composition ability was not systematically evaluated.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in five relevant categories. The authors’ public launch thread showed 13.2K views when checked, a visible but author-posted reach signal rather than independent validation; the project also has an accessible technical site.

sections.title: WebHarbor: Docking Real Websites for Evolving GUI Agent Environments
sections.abstract: The authors introduce 153 deterministic, Dockerized website environments and 3,518 tasks—including post-authentication workflows—built through human-agent collaboration for GUI-agent evaluation and reinforcement learning.
sections.claimed_contribution: The arXiv abstract reports that an RL-trained 4B-level GUI agent generalizes to unseen tasks and is competitive with leading open-source web agents across four benchmarks.
sections.unique_caveat: The environments are task-driven replicas, not complete live websites; reported benchmark transfer does not establish fidelity across the open-ended, changing web. The authors describe human review as part of environment construction.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The cross-list spans three core AI categories; a separate technical discussion examines its reproducibility-versus-fidelity trade-off, and the authors provide a public project site and repository. These sources do not establish readership or citation counts.

sections.title: Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents
sections.abstract: Strategist uses executable, reusable reasoning-strategy blueprints and a growing library to search and refine inference strategies; on 30 benchmarks, the authors report matching the strongest baseline’s average accuracy (74.7% versus 74.0%) at 39% lower inference cost.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors describe a strategy-design loop that accumulates reusable blueprints across tasks instead of starting over for each benchmark.
sections.unique_caveat: Transfer is not uniform: the paper reports losses on some benchmarks and mixed accuracy/cost outcomes across GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5; results depend on the benchmark samples and model configurations evaluated.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The arXiv record identifies NeurIPS 2026, and the work has appeared in multiple paper-discovery summaries; its full experimental HTML is available for direct checking.

sections.title: DeliverBench: Benchmarking AI Agents on Delivering Realistic Multi-Stage Professional Projects
sections.abstract: DeliverBench evaluates agents across 11 expert-reconstructed projects in finance, legal drafting, and drug-safety reporting, chaining 150 subtasks through feedback rounds; the authors report that the best of seven systems scores 65/100 on final delivery.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors use expert rubrics at intermediate checkpoints and final delivery to expose errors carried across stages; their abstract reports only a 50% subtask pass rate at a 90-point threshold for the best system.
sections.unique_caveat: The benchmark contains 11 projects in three professional areas, so it cannot by itself establish performance across the breadth of professional work; expert rubric judgments are central to its scoring.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The benchmark received separate write-ups at The Latest in AI and Turing Wire, providing checkable discussion beyond the arXiv listing. These are coverage signals, not measured readership or citations.

sections.title: DepthGraft: Structural Regularization through Hierarchical Cross-Layer KV Reconstruction
sections.abstract: DepthGraft reconstructs deep-layer key/value representations from shallower and middle-layer pairs, with the authors reporting roughly one-third less KV cache and downstream gains across dense and mixture-of-experts models up to 16B parameters.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors interpret cross-layer KV reuse as both cache sharing and a structural gradient path, then propose hierarchical reuse; they report a 7-point absolute MMLU-Pro improvement for their 16B MoE setting.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported evidence is bounded to the tested 0.5B–16B dense/MoE models and listed downstream benchmarks; larger-scale and deployment behavior is not established by the abstract’s results.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The work has a NeurIPS 2026 poster record, an externally checkable venue signal. Its abstract reports evaluations across multiple model sizes and attention configurations; no public engagement count was verified.
